stories.summary: A fawn races in the forest and stumbles on a boulder, hurting his leg. With the help of his animal friends and mother, they come up with a solution to comfort him.
A fat king and his thin dog go for a walk. The dog chases a bird, leading to a comical chase that ends with the king becoming thin.

The story explores the unseen presence of Vayu, the Wind, in everyday occurrences like cooling down after a bath, making milk ready to drink, and causing curtains to flutter. Through poetic verses, the narrator ponders on the mysterious and invisible actions of the wind.

Chuskit, a young girl with a disability, dreams of going to school like her brother. With the help of a thoughtful classmate, the school community comes together to make the path accessible for Chuskit, allowing her to attend school for the first time.
A child keeps asking to do things but is told to wait by the adults. Eventually, they are granted all their wishes on their birthday.

Moru, a boy with strong likes and dislikes, stops going to school after a conflict with his teacher. Instead, he spends his time doing mischievous activities until a new teacher arrives with colorful books. Moru rediscovers his love for numbers and learning, eventually returning to school and helping other children with their studies.

A child decides to spend the day listening to their body, exploring the sounds and sensations it makes. They engage in various activities to hear their breath, heart, and stomach, finding joy in the experience.
Kicchu and Choru go fishing at the pond, but a funny mishap occurs when they both try to catch the same fish, leading to a surprising twist.
Susheela loves making kolams and gets a special request from the Air Force to create one in the sky. She helps the pilots draw a beautiful kolam that lights up the city.

Pehelwaan Ji, a strong character, is challenged to a wrestling match by Gappu. However, when Gappu tickles him, Pehelwaan Ji ends up dancing and running away, showing a humorous side to his tough persona.

source.title: Sister, Sister, Where Does the Sun Go at Night?
source.author: Roopa Pai

stories.summary: A little brother and sister wonder where the sun goes at night, sharing imaginative ideas until the sister explains the scientific reality of the earth's rotation causing day and night.
Meenu celebrates Vasant Panchami, the first day of spring, with her family. She learns about the season, plants a tree with her grandpa, and enjoys the beauty of nature around her.
Anu is excited to meet Aunty Jui's baby but gets disappointed when she finds the baby is just a small infant. Anu tries to act like a baby herself but realizes being a big sister is more fun.
Anil wants something from the market but keeps choosing items that will cause trouble. After a series of mishaps, he finally picks a puppy without causing any chaos.

The story follows a child experiencing winter and various winter-related activities and festivals in different parts of India. From Groundnut Fair to Snowman Competition, the child learns about different traditions and foods associated with the season.

source.title: Kheer on a Full Moon Night
source.author: Mala Kumar, Manisha Chaudhry

stories.summary: The story follows a child experiencing various festivals and traditions during the autumn season, including Sharat Poornima, Onam, Navaratri Golu, and Deepavali. The child learns about different customs, enjoys celebrations, and looks forward to the changing seasons.

The story describes a child's experiences during the monsoon season, enjoying the rain, observing nature, and savoring homemade food. It also touches on Indian classical music and cultural traditions.

The story follows Goloo the circle, a personified shape, as it describes all the places and objects where it can be found in everyday life. From the sun to fruits to playground games, Goloo is everywhere except on report cards.
Uncle Sandy embarks on a quest to find a mysterious cat in the Western Ghats, encountering various animals and learning about the importance of wildlife conservation along the way.
Rani goes to school for the first time with her mother. She feels nervous but eventually finds the courage to go inside alone, knowing her mother will be there when she comes out.
Nanhi wants to draw a long train but runs out of space on her slate. She continues drawing on the floor until her chalk finishes, creating a train that stretches the length of the verandah.

Tullu and Bullu, twin rabbits living in a jungle, encounter a wolf seeking warmth. Despite the wolf's deceitful intentions, the clever rabbits outsmart him with boiling water and live happily ever after.
Shanti comes to school looking sad and not smiling. Her friends try to figure out why until Arun surprises her with a rubber frog, making her laugh and revealing the reason behind her frown.
In a town known for cricket bat manufacturing, a missing bat causes a stir at Rehman Chacha's factory. After a comical investigation, the mystery is solved in a surprising and humorous way.
The story lists various things that different animals and people can't do, leading to a humorous and surprising conclusion.

Bulbuli embarks on a journey to Senseless Point with her parrot friend Totaram and an elephant named Hathi to end the war between the jungles. Through understanding and unity, she discovers the unique fragrances of tea, tulsi, and elaichi, leading to the creation of a refreshing new tea blend.
A child and their family are going to a wedding in the village by train. They wait at the station, meet other family members, and finally board the train when the groom arrives.

A child hurries to get home after school, navigating through busy streets with various shops and traffic. After a close encounter with a street vendor, the child finally reaches home to spend time with family.
Timmy teases his puppy, Pepe, by pointing out body parts he has. Pepe responds with 'woof' each time, until Timmy mentions hands, which Pepe doesn't have. Despite the teasing, they love each other.

A child explores the sounds around them, from the cheep of sparrows to the drip of a tap, and wonders why others can't hear them. Through curiosity and discovery, the child finds a world full of hidden sounds waiting to be explored.
Children creatively play with a crumpled paper, turning it into various objects like a ball, lollipop, boat, and camera, leading to laughter and fun.

Suraj plays with his special ball named Sher Singh in the park. The ball, personified as a tiger, goes on a series of playful adventures, getting picked up by a dog, pinching a boy, and rolling through a play tunnel before reuniting with Suraj.

Veeru goes to the circus with his grandparents and dreams of having his own circus. He invites his family to 'Veeru Circus' and performs various acts, making adjustments to ensure safety, and ends the show with laughter and joy.

Gauri helps her mother make scarecrows, but at night the scarecrows come to life and dress up in pretty clothes, leading to a fun parade. When birds start eating the grain, the scarecrows scare them away, and Gauri wakes up to find the scarecrows back in place.
Anu loves to observe and see patterns in everyday things around her, from nature to objects in her home. She finds joy in the simple beauty of the world.
The animals in the jungle discover a school and explore it, looking for their teacher. They hear a roar and get scared, but it turns out to be their teacher, a lion.

The story follows a child and their brother at their school, the balwadi. They engage in various activities like counting, playing with toys, reading books, and listening to stories told with puppets. The day ends with the school bell ringing and the children going home with their mother.

A young prince takes a walk among the trees in the royal orchard with his father, the King. They explore different fruit trees like pomegranate, jackfruit, papaya, banana, and more, learning about their characteristics and uses.

source.title: Sister, Sister, Where Does Thunder Come From?
source.author: Roopa Pai

stories.summary: A little brother and sister wonder where thunder comes from, sharing imaginative stories involving a sleeping giant, a gang of bikers, and children playing a game in the sky. The sister finally explains the scientific process behind thunder and lightning.

The story follows different body parts of a child as they talk about their abilities and senses, inviting the reader to be their friend. Each body part describes how they function and interact with the world around them.

source.title: Sister, Sister Why is the Sky So Blue?
source.author: Roopa Pai

stories.summary: A brother and sister wonder why the sky is blue, coming up with imaginative and creative explanations. They discuss various theories until the sister explains the scientific reason behind the blue sky.

source.title: Sister, Sister, Why Don't Things Fall Up?
source.author: Roopa Pai

stories.summary: A brother and sister wonder why things don't fall up and share imaginative stories about it. Through their conversation, they explore different theories until they learn about gravity and how it keeps everything on Earth from falling up.

Ramya receives diamond star earrings from her Grandma, who claims to have taken the stars from the sky. Feeling sad, Ramya dreams of a fairy returning the stars to the sky, and wakes up to find the night sky filled with stars, making her happy.
The protagonist struggles with finding the right clothes to wear, each item causing some sort of trouble. Eventually, they decide to mix and match to create their own unique style.
Maaloo is collecting vegetables from the garden for the first time but can't find any potatoes. With the help of his dog Kaaloo, they discover the potatoes hidden in the mud and fill their basket.

Bunty loves to play with butterflies, birds, paper boats, and sand castles. When she refuses to clean up at home, she has a dream where germs attack her castle. With the help of Soap King Bubbly and his army of bubbles, Bunty learns the importance of cleanliness.
A child describes their home and the daily activities that take place there with their family, from hanging clothes to cooking food and welcoming guests.

source.title: Kaka and Munni: A Folktale from Punjab
source.author: Natasha Sharma

stories.summary: Munni the sparrow outsmarts the village bully, Kaka the crow, by cleverly diverting his attention and getting him involved in a series of tasks. In the end, Kaka's vanity leads to his own downfall, and Munni's eggs are saved.
Sringeri Srinivas has too many bananas that nobody wants. He seeks help and surprises everyone by turning the bananas into delicious banana halwa packets, solving the problem of excess bananas.

Loco, a timid train, overcomes its fears with the help of the wise old train, Babu the engine driver, and the guard on its maiden journey from Tamil Nadu to Jammu. Along the way, Loco discovers its own bravery and learns not to be afraid of anything.
Veena and Vinay help painters paint a gate in their garden, accidentally creating a two-colored gate in the process.
A child loses their cap in the wind, but the moon helps by trying it on and sending a new one. The child and the moon both wear their caps happily.

A child goes through their morning routine, expressing reluctance for each task at first but eventually changing their mind after considering the positive aspects. The story ends with the child eagerly getting ready for a class picnic at the zoo.
The story explores the preferences between straight and curly things, from hair to roads, in a repetitive and cozy manner.

Tinku, unable to sleep, ventures out into the night and makes new friends with nocturnal animals like a firefly, bat, fox, owl, and cricket. He learns about their nighttime activities and the beauty of the night before returning home to sleep peacefully.

Ritu helps Grandpa write a letter to invite Mani for the holidays. She eagerly posts the letter herself but adds multiple 'please' to it. Eventually, Mani's visit is confirmed, and Ritu learns about the power of politeness.

Basava and Sundari eagerly wait for their sailor father to return home. They visit the beach every morning, hoping to see his ship. When they learn a ship from Kamboja has arrived, they go to the jetty to find out more.
The story follows the playful interactions between a child named Bekku and the narrator, highlighting their differences in preferences and actions but their shared love for milk.

Sringeri Srinivas faces a dilemma when no one in the village can cut his long hair on Annual Haircut Day. After a series of failed attempts, a surprising encounter with a tiger resolves his problem in a unique way.
Meenu spends the summer learning about different foods and traditions with her family and friends. She also takes care of a sapling, hoping it will grow into a fruit-bearing tree.
Bheema loves to sleep but struggles to wake up early. Various animals try to help him wake up, but it's a fly that finally succeeds by making him sneeze.
Golu the elephant and Chhotu the rabbit play a game where they take turns leaping on each other's backs, leading to a funny mishap with falling coconuts.

The story describes the various types of friends the child has, including older, younger, tiny, those with tails, those that fly, and those that swim. In the end, the child's best friend is revealed to be their mother.

Khaidi, a seven-year-old, enjoys driving the car his Papa made for his birthday. He goes on various adventures with his car, visiting relatives, driving around the earth, and even around the sun, moon, and stars. Despite some mishaps, Khaidi and his little brother continue to have fun with the car.

A child searches all over the house for a lost yo-yo, but can't find it. Granny returns from a walk and surprises the child by finding the yo-yo in the park. They spend the day playing with the yo-yo together.

Arjun, an auto-rickshaw, dreams of flying and experiences a magical journey through the city with his driver and a passenger. As they soar above Delhi, they discover the true magic of life and the importance of family and purpose.
Manu eagerly waits for the rain to come so he can wear his new red raincoat, asking his mother about the weather each day until the rain finally arrives.

Bani, a little girl, falls asleep and finds herself in a magical world filled with talking mushrooms, flying children, and toy mountains. She explores this whimsical place, enjoying laddoos, mushroom chips, and lemonade, before returning home to her own bed.
The story describes various colorful objects in nature, each engaging in whimsical activities. The narrative is presented in a rhyming and poetic style.

source.title: Happy and Sad (Tell me now series)
source.author: Madhav Chavan

stories.summary: The story explores different emotions experienced by various characters in everyday situations, with questions posed and answered about their feelings.
The story follows a child asking questions about different colors and receiving simple explanations for each. It explores common questions about colors and their origins.

source.title: Naughty or Not (Tell me now series)
source.author: Madhav Chavan

stories.summary: The story explores questions about behavior and self-esteem through a series of interactions between characters.
Gulli helps family members with everyday problems by finding useful items in his box of things, like a magnifying glass, a funnel, and a magnet.

Paplu, a giant child, is taken to a village where he befriends the locals. When a bandit threatens the village, Paplu must remember a magic chant to regain his giant size and save the day. With the help of the villagers, he defeats the bandits and becomes known as Paplu, the Giant.

Cheenu eagerly waits for his father, a junk dealer, to pick him up from school. Together, they collect newspapers, magazines, and more items from different places. In the end, Cheenu's father surprises him with a book as a gift.

source.title: Kallu's World 1 - In Big Trouble Again!
source.author: Subhadra Sen Gupta

stories.summary: Kallu struggles to get to school on time and faces the threat of serious consequences if he's late again. He frantically tries to come up with a convincing excuse for his tardiness, only to discover he's actually early, leading to a humorous misunderstanding with his teacher.

source.title: The Day the Vegetables Came to School
source.author: Venkatramana Gowda

stories.summary: Raju has a dream where vegetables come to school in a parade, surprising everyone. He wakes up to realize it was just a dream and gets ready for school.

Kaage the crow tries to learn singing, dancing, and nest-building from other birds but fails. Eventually, she discovers her talent for sharing food and being generous, making her proud to be part of a crow family.

source.title: The Woodcutter of Gura - A Folktale from Ethiopia
source.author: Veena Seshadri

stories.summary: The woodcutter of Gura chops wood in a dangerous way, leading to a series of misunderstandings that make him believe he is dead. His friends and wife think he is dead until he finally gets up and proves them wrong.

source.title: Three for Free - A Folktale from Taiwan
source.author: Greystroke

stories.summary: An old man sells delicious dumplings in a village, offering three for free. The villagers' greed leads to a surprising revelation about the mountain and the old man's true identity as a mountain god.
A dog wants to catch a bird but learns a lesson from a man. The man helps the dog understand the importance of not chasing birds.
Amma visits Meera's school and gets caught up in a humorous chain of events involving a snake that leads to confusion and chaos.

Grandpa Fish, head of the fish family, struggles to listen to the news on their prized radio due to the younger ones' love for film music. When he finally hears a warning about humans poisoning rivers, he takes action to protect his community with the help of the village headman.

A cloud brings rain to a dry land, fulfilling the wishes of various creatures and people, including a peacock, fish, farmer, and a boy named Raju. The rain brings joy and fun to everyone before moving on.
Devi's little sister gets stuck in a flying cradle, and her friends try various ways to bring her down before Devi's father arrives.

source.title: The Magic Powder - A Folktale from Myanmar
source.author: Greystroke

stories.summary: Thuza's husband believes he can turn dirt into gold through alchemy. With the help of her wise father, they trick him into thinking he has succeeded by using magic powder from banana leaves. In the end, he learns the true value of hard work and perseverance.

Raza, a young boy, accompanies his father, the royal tailor, to meet King Akbar. They present the king with new clothes, but struggle to find the right belt. Raza suggests using a turban as a belt, impressing the king with his creativity and knowledge of designs.

Vikki, a squirrel, convinces his cousin Kato to go on a boat ride despite Kato's fear of water. During the ride, Kato falls into the river but is rescued by a swan, leading to an exciting adventure for the two squirrels.

Gubbi the sparrow loses her guava in a clump of thorns and seeks help from various animals to get it back. After a series of requests, the ant finally helps her by orchestrating a chain of events that lead to the guava's return. However, Gubbi's greed leads to an unexpected punishment.

Dhani, a young boy living in Mahatma Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram, learns about the historic Dandi March to protest against the British tax on salt. Despite his eagerness to join, he realizes his responsibility to care for his goat, Binni, while the march takes place.

Two siblings receive money from their grandfather to buy books. They struggle to decide which books to buy at the small bookshop but with the help of the shopkeeper, they finally make their choices and enjoy reading together.

Shobhini and Nani have various everyday adventures together, from visiting a mela to combing hair, going to the jungle, playing in the rain, rolling wool, bathing in the river, and even taking a trip to the moon on Nani's special walking stick.

Samira goes shopping for sooji but gets distracted by a butterfly, a cat, flowers, and gets lost. With the help of her dog Mouchak, she finds her way back home just in time for her birthday celebration.

source.title: Sniffles, the Crocodile and Punch, the Butterfly
source.author: Herminder Ohri

stories.summary: Sniffles, a crocodile who doesn't want to eat other animals, befriends Punch, a butterfly. When Punch warns Sniffles of men coming to kill crocodiles, they work together to scare the men away, with the help of other crocodiles and butterflies.

After the Great Race, the hare and the tortoise are sent on a mission by the king of the jungle. They must work together to overcome obstacles and successfully complete their task in the neighboring kingdom.

source.title: Here Comes the Camel and Other Poems
source.author: Prayag Shukla

stories.summary: A collection of poems describing everyday scenes like a butterfly, elephant, school, and food. Each poem paints a vivid picture of simple, delightful moments.
A young child learns to climb up on things but struggles to climb back down. With encouragement from Papa, the child overcomes the fear and successfully climbs down from the table and chair.

Chandu dreams of flying and meets various flying creatures like a butterfly, sparrow, eagle, and even an aeroplane and a rocket. He feels great and part of the stars before being woken up by his mother.
Rumniya gets lost at a wedding, but with her clever thinking, she manages to find her way back to her Nani. The story highlights the bond between a grandchild and grandparent.
A young boy explores his creativity by drawing and making things, but faces challenges when his sister makes a mess. Despite this, he continues to create various objects and drawings.

source.title: I lost my bat! I found my bat!
source.author: Meera Tendolkar

stories.summary: A child searches for their lost bat in various places around the house, but can't seem to find it. After looking everywhere, they finally discover where the bat was hiding.
A mouse causes chaos in the house as each family member tries to catch it, leading to a humorous chase around the house until the baby ends up befriending the mouse.

Shyam, a ten-year-old boy, daydreams about what life would be like if his body parts were different sizes. From a long neck to strong arms, he explores various imaginative scenarios before being brought back to reality by his mother.

Samira refuses to eat her lunch of parathas and brinjal curry, finding fault with every alternative offered by animals and insects in the school garden. Eventually, she realizes her lunch isn't so bad after all and happily eats it.
The lion, king of the jungle, suffers from a toothache. Various animals suggest ways to help, but it's the wise little mouse who ultimately solves the problem by cleaning the lion's teeth.

source.title: Monkey Business on Stage - Kallu's World 2
source.author: Subhadra Sen Gupta

stories.summary: In Khajuria village, the annual Ramlila preparations are in full swing. Kallu and his friends eagerly participate in the play, with unexpected and hilarious results.
Sona wants to help her mother make prints on a sari. While working together, Sona listens carefully and uses her observation skills to help her mother find the missing keys.
Sringeri Srinivas, a farmer, is bothered by the loud noises around him. He seeks silence and finally finds it with the help of headphones, bringing peace back to his life.

Phani is always late for school because his chappals have a mind of their own and take him on unexpected adventures. Despite his explanations, nobody believes him until his mother surprises him with a new pair of chappals.

A child wakes up to find everything in their room behaving strangely, from objects growing and moving to animals acting out of character. A magic man appears to fix the chaos and restore order with a spell.
A young girl faces her fears as she encounters various sounds and sights around her home, realizing there is nothing to be afraid of.
A big girl enjoys helping her family members with various tasks, but sometimes they ask her not to help. She finds solace in reading a book and spending time with her grandmother.

source.title: Wailers Three - A Folktale From China
source.author: Greystroke

stories.summary: Old Mrs. Chang receives a letter from her son in Beijing but can't read it. Warrior Wen, who also can't read, tries to help but ends up crying. The story unfolds with a series of misunderstandings and reveals the importance of literacy.

King Petuchand is disturbed by a mysterious tok-tok sound in the palace. After a comical search, they discover a tiny bird causing the noise. The bird is relocated to the border to keep the soldiers awake, becoming the official bird of the country.

The story follows a child experiencing common health issues like a runny nose and sore throat, questioning why these things happen. Through simple rhymes, the child explores solutions like wiping their nose and blowing up a balloon.

Pehelwaan ji, a strong wrestler, tries to play cricket with the children but his strength causes chaos on the field. After a series of mishaps, he realizes cricket isn't for him and leaves, allowing the children to continue playing peacefully.

Anaya loves sucking her thumb but wonders if she could put it to better use after seeing baby animals sucking on different body parts at the zoo. She decides to let go of her thumb and have fun like the other children.

Saboo meets a giraffe named Jojo in the garden and goes on an adventure around town, attending a birthday party and having fun. They return home, surprising Saboo's mother, who thought he wanted a small puppy.

Two friends, Kindru-Lalim and Kincha Lali-Dam, seek advice from animals in the forest to build the first house. With guidance from an elephant, snake, mithun, and fish, they successfully construct a house that they share with the creatures of the forest.

A child wakes up thirsty at night and thinks there's a tiger under the bed, only to discover it's just their sweater. With the help of their mother, they realize there was nothing to fear and go back to sleep.

Nani keeps losing her glasses, and the child protagonist helps her search by following clues from Nani's day. After a thorough investigation, the missing glasses are found in unexpected places around the house.
A child has a special friend who lives inside the mirror. They play together in the child's dreams, bringing joy and fun.

The story follows a line of ants as they go about their daily activities, showcasing their unique communication through smells and their strength. The ants also teach the reader about opposites and the concept of hard work.
The story follows a cat living in a house with its family and best friend. It describes the cat's daily activities, interactions with other animals, and how it keeps itself clean without water.

A crow living in a mango tree shares its daily activities, from eating ripe fruit to looking for food and sharing with friends. The story also introduces the sounds different animals make and compares loud talking to noisy crows.

A family of four, including a responsible older sibling and a mischievous younger one, share their daily activities and responsibilities. The story highlights the bond between siblings and the importance of looking out for each other.
A boy asks for a drum but receives a piece of wood instead. Through a series of kind acts, he ends up with a drum, teaching the value of giving and sharing.

Munia, a brave girl with a limp, befriends a giant one-feathered elephant bird living near her village. When the village's horse goes missing, suspicion falls on the bird. Munia sets out to solve the mystery and proves the innocence of her friend.

A child compares themselves to various animals, pointing out similarities and differences in features and abilities. Ultimately, they realize that humans are also animals and that they all belong together.

source.title: The Boy and the Drum (A Shorter Version)
source.author: Umesh P N

stories.summary: A boy's mother couldn't afford a drum, so he sets off with a piece of wood. Along the way, he helps various people in need, receiving items in return. Eventually, he ends up with a drum through his acts of kindness.

Pishi, a manta ray, gets injured during a storm and must find his friends and get help. With the assistance of cleaner fish at a cleaning station, Pishi's wound is treated, and he is able to recover and appreciate the beauty of the Indian Ocean.

Sukhiya Kaka, a singer from Bitauna village, meets a dinosaur named Dinoo and they sing together in the rain, bringing joy to the village of Jhalaura. They share an umbrella and enjoy the rain while following the scent of delicious pakoras.

Tara embarks on a solo journey to her ancestral village, encountering various modes of transportation and nature along the way. She ends her day under the stars, reflecting on her adventure and the warmth of home.
Spot, a circle, and Spike, a triangle, have a humorous conversation about their shapes. When they spot what they think is a shark, they realize it's just each other's shapes causing a scare.
Baby Thangwang and Bhalluka the bear like to talk to each other. When Thangwang loses his little red toy, Bhalluka helps him find it in a funny and heartwarming way.
A child describes their granny who loves to juggle everything she can find, causing chaos and laughter wherever she goes. Despite the mess, the family enjoys her unique talent and the joy it brings.
A child blames a series of events on a cat getting stuck in a tree, leading to a chain reaction that results in the dog eating the child's homework.
A child explores the world, wondering who made it, with a mysterious tone. The story takes the reader across rivers, cities, forests, and hills, ending with a question about the creator of the world.

A young girl imagines herself as the Lantern Queen after a lantern appears above her head. Through her day, she learns valuable lessons about responsibility, hygiene, and making a positive impact on others.
A monkey sneaks in through the window and eats fruits, while a cat eats fruits in the garden.

An 89-year-old lady loves juggling and decides to fulfill her dream of juggling at her great grandson's school. Chaos ensues when she juggles with the children's belongings, but it all ends well with an invitation to perform on the annual day.

source.title: My Diwali Book
source.author: Rakhee Iyer
source.illustrator: Gayathri Manikandan, Priya Kuriyan, Taposhi Ghoshal

stories.summary: A child learns about the Festival of Lights, Diwali, and its significance. They help prepare for the celebration by making traditional food, decorating the house, and lighting diyas and sparklers.

Mili wants a different kind of birthday celebration, so her family decorates their home like it's Deepavali. The neighborhood joins in, and they have a festive celebration with traditional decorations, games, and sweets.

Vihaan, a baby who can't talk, starts crying until BooBoo Bear and his pet mushroom MushyMushy come to cheer him up. After a mishap with the mushroom, Vihaan cries again until BooBoo suggests singing a silly song, which brings laughter to everyone.

Toto, who loves animals, discovers that Gogo the gorilla is missing from his cage at the zoo. He sets off on an adventure to find him, searching through the jungle and even diving into a river before finally locating Gogo happily munching on bananas in a nearby store.
Ammu pretends to have a puppy named Shankar, but when her friends want to visit, she gets caught in her lie. However, a surprise awaits her in the garden that brings joy and laughter.

Malu and Moidootty try to summon a demon to get mangoes, but it goes wrong and a scary demon threatens to eat everything. With the help of their grandmother, they outsmart the demon and save the day by making it rain, causing the demon to disappear.

A little boy wakes up to find a strange blue man and a water buffalo in his living room, trying to take his mother's soul. The boy's mother reveals that her soul is with him, leading to a mysterious and magical encounter that ends with the blue man leaving empty-handed.

source.title: The Princess and the Veggy Lion
source.author: Uma Balamurali
source.illustrator: Ajit Narayan, Ketan Raut, Padmanabh, Preeti Krishnamurthy, Rayika Sen, Sanjay Sarkar, Tapas Guha..

stories.summary: A Princess gets lost in the forest and encounters a veggy lion who helps her find her way back to the palace with the assistance of an elephant. They all become friends and live happily together.
Percy, a little elephant, learns a lesson when the ants he carelessly steps on decide to tickle him until he says sorry.
Subami introduces her family members, all with names starting with 'S'. They spend a cozy day together at home, appreciating each other's company and the simple joys of everyday life.

source.title: My Musical Adventure
source.author: Anush-Adi Navaneeth
source.illustrator: Ajit Narayan, Madhuri Purandare, Preeti Krishnamurthy, Priya Kuriyan, Rijuta Ghate, Vibhash Pandey

stories.summary: Savitri, a young girl with a passion for singing, embarks on a musical adventure that takes her to different places to learn various styles of music. Along the way, she discovers her talent, enjoys learning, and eventually wins a singing competition, all while eagerly awaiting the arrival of her new baby sibling.

source.title: Asha gives up a bad habit!
source.author: Geetha Ravi

stories.summary: Asha, a clever girl, has a bad habit of chewing pencils. Her parents and teacher try to help her break the habit. A visit to a pencil factory and a lesson on the importance of trees changes Asha's perspective.

source.title: The puppy that did not bark!!!
source.author: Uma Balamurali
source.illustrator: Deepa Balsavar, Greystroke, Madhuri Purandare, Natasha Sharma, Preeti Krishnamurthy, Priya Kuriyan, Santosh Pujari, Soumya Menon, Suvidha Mistry

stories.summary: Rinku finds a puppy in the bushes near her house and secretly keeps it as her pet. She tries to teach the puppy to bark with the help of her friends and finally succeeds with the help of a white dog.

source.title: Preetha Aunty- My teacher
source.author: Arthi Anand-Navaneeth
source.illustrator: Greystroke, Herminder Ohri, Rijuta Ghate, Sheetal Thapa, Soumya Menon

stories.summary: A child learns Hindi with their teacher Preetha Aunty, starting from letters and progressing to words. On the child's birthday, they share chocolates with friends and teachers, including Preetha Aunty.

source.title: The Cave Party
source.author: Shrey Dave
source.illustrator: Angie & Upesh, Muniza Shariq, Padmanabh, Santosh Pujari

stories.summary: A tiger lives in a cave and scares off visitors with his loud roar. When a deer comes in looking for water, a lion and an elephant join the party, leading to a fun celebration.
A child climbs a big tree near their house and enjoys hopping at the top. Despite interruptions from their mother, the child continues to climb and hop, leading to a playful and silly adventure.
A child enjoys flying their strong kite with their father's help, imagining flying it even in the rain.

A Techdroid named D-56 discovers Crocobots causing trouble at the factory. Through a series of events, including a river adventure and an underwater city, they find out the Crocobots are actually friendly droids in disguise.
A cat named Margaret Mallikarjun Chulli-cat surprises everyone by pooping out stories after eating. The humorous tale follows the antics of the cat and the reactions of those around her.

normalizations: story_type: no valid values, coerced to ['other']

stories.summary: Didi visits a group of children who live near a garbage dump and introduces them to colorful books. The children learn to read and decide to find Didi when she falls ill, bringing joy back into her life.
A poem personifying litter and its harmful effects on the environment, urging readers to take responsibility and protect the planet from pollution and disease.
The story emphasizes the importance of not wasting food and sharing with those in need. It highlights the impact of kindness and generosity towards others.
Various animals describe what makes them special, from shiny shells to sweet voices. Finally, a boy realizes that being himself is what truly makes him special.

source.title: Jaggee's mornings
source.author: Sandhya Sridhar
source.illustrator: Angie & Upesh, Hari Kumar Nair, Rajiv Eipe, Rijuta Ghate, Shailja Jain Chougule, Suvidha Mistry, Tapas Guha

stories.summary: Jaggee struggles to wake up in the mornings for school but finds joy and comfort once he is there, surrounded by friends and teachers he loves.

source.title: Tree on a plate
source.author: Madhuri Pai
source.illustrator: Ajit Narayan, Angie & Upesh, Henu, Padmanabh, Rijuta Ghate, Suvidha Mistry

stories.summary: Roma enjoys dinner time and imagines her food as different landscapes on her plate, like a hill made of rice, a yellow lake of dal, and a forest with a 'tree vegetable' that looks like a cauliflower.

source.title: Fun with Balloon
source.author: Madhuri Pai
source.illustrator: Ajit Narayan, Greystroke, Shailja Jain Chougule

stories.summary: Bittu and Kittu play together and have fun blowing up a small ball that turns into a big balloon, bringing laughter and joy.

source.title: My Friend Trace Roger the robot!
source.author: Baani Pahwa
source.illustrator: Greystroke, Nirvaan Pahwa, Ruchi Shah, Vibhash Pandey

stories.summary: A child discovers a broken robot in the store room and with the help of family, fixes it. The robot becomes a fun companion but causes a mishap, leading to a teamwork solution with the child's grandma.

Tiya and her pet elephant Tofu participate in a running competition where Tofu initially gets scared due to the size of the other elephants. With Tiya's encouragement, Tofu overcomes his fear and wins the race, learning that trying is better than being scared.

Nadir, a lively boy from Adyar, Chennai, finds a horse named Faraz and they have many adventures together. When Faraz is stolen by thieves, Nadir takes quick action to rescue him with the help of the police.
Ramu drops some sweets, attracting a line of ants who work together to carry the treats back to their home. The ants share a feast that night, teaching Ramu about sharing.

source.title: Long Water
source.author: Madhuri Pai
source.illustrator: Herminder Ohri, Sanjay Sarkar, Santosh Pujari, Sonal Goyal, Sumit Sakhuja

stories.summary: The story personifies a river, describing its characteristics and functions in a repetitive manner, leading to the reveal of its identity through clues.

Stripey the Bee, who doesn't know how to make honey, goes on a journey to discover the secret behind it. After searching and learning from a magic book, Stripey finally learns how to make honey and becomes self-sufficient.

source.title: The Rainbow Story
source.author: Prakruti & Shruti Bhat
source.illustrator: Ajit Narayan, Bulbul Sharma, Deepa Balsavar, Greystroke, Lavanya Karthik, Niloufer Wadia, Nimret Handa, Priya Kuriyan, Sanjay Sarkar

stories.summary: Prakruti and her Ajji receive colorful gifts from Kalia the crow each day of the week, leading to a beautiful rainbow being painted in the sky for Kalia to enjoy.
Prakruti learns about the concept of nature from her grandmother, Ajji, through a poetic exploration of the elements and beauty of the natural world.

source.title: Animals Are Kind
source.author: Preksha Pc
source.illustrator: Ajit Narayan, Padmanabh, Rijuta Ghate, Sanjay Sarkar

stories.summary: A farmer dislikes birds, but his son Sanju loves them. When Sanju gets hurt and no one is around to help, a bird he helped in the past comes to his aid, leading to a change of heart for the farmer.

source.title: The boy who hated vegetables
source.author: Prakruti & Shruti Bhat
source.illustrator: Angie & Upesh, Deepa Balsavar, Padmanabh, Rijuta Ghate, Suvidha Mistry, Tanvi Choudhury

stories.summary: Chinnu, a boy who loves chocolates, refuses to eat vegetables until he has a dream where his vegetable friends follow him to school. Scared by the dream, he decides to start eating vegetables and ends up loving them.

Twins Sara and Zara long for a merry-go-round, but are disappointed when they can't find one at the circus. Their older sister tries to cheer them up to no avail. Eventually, they stumble upon a merry-go-round at the local park and have the best day ever.
Aloke, a cheerful boy, dreams of a happy dinosaur who loves nature. Despite his mom's warnings, he enjoys the rain and shares his happiness with a little frog.

Tammy the turtle goes on a journey to find her mother after getting separated. Along the way, she encounters various sea creatures and experiences magical moments, eventually reuniting with her mother.

source.title: Tina and the crazy animal
source.author: Rachita Uday Kumar
source.illustrator: Sonal Goyal, Sumit Sakhuja, Sumit Sakhuja

stories.summary: Tina, a mischievous girl, sneaks into the forest and befriends a crazy animal. When the villagers try to harm the animal, Tina stands up for her friend, proving that the animal means no harm.

Kaushik, a young boy, sets out with his new detective tools to explore the forest near his farm. He discovers a tiny girl named Lalitha who lives in the forest with her family and learns about their unique way of staying dry during the rain. Kaushik offers to teach them how to build a house, ending his detective adventure and beginning a new friendship.

source.title: Richard's unlucky day
source.author: Lotte Van Oijen
source.illustrator: Angie & Upesh, Deepa Balsavar, Greystroke, Lavanya Karthik, Rijuta Ghate

stories.summary: Richard has a series of unlucky events in his day, from cold water in the shower to no breakfast and rain outside. Despite the mishaps, he ends up enjoying a delicious cake with his family.
A boy exploring near mushrooms finds a small girl under a magic spell. He helps her return to normal size after a conversation with his mother.
Timmi dreams of having a dog and eventually gets one. She teaches her new pet various tricks until her dream finally comes true.
A child enjoys hiding their grandmother's spectacles, leading to scoldings and moments of fun. They help her find the glasses and try to knit her a sweater, ending the day by singing her a song.

Toku, a jungle boy, receives an invitation to Nela the horse's birthday party. Along with his animal friends, they journey to the party, meeting new friends along the way. The party is filled with fun activities and is a memorable experience for all.
Mr. Fish has been sleeping for 2 days and 2 hours, causing concern for the sender of the letter. The reason for Mr. Fish's extended nap is revealed to be a lack of fish food.
A group of animals in the forest hold a race to determine the fastest animal. After a thrilling competition, Cheek the cheetah emerges as the winner, proving to be the fastest of them all.
In a magical jungle, an elephant named Jumbo couldn't talk or sing like the other animals. Despite being teased, he trained hard for a running race in the zoo and proved everyone wrong by winning.

A folklore Singer in Rajasthan befriends a Dinosaur skeleton and brings it to life with a life-giving song. Together, they sing a folklore song about rain, which miraculously brings rain to the region after a long dry spell.

Olivia's parents disappear in a war, and she embarks on a magical quest to find them based on riddles in a mysterious book. With determination and skill, she overcomes challenges in a maze, fairy land, and a magic patch to reunite with her parents in India.
Sheela, a shy girl, learns to make friends with her shadow Leela in a magical forest adventure. Together, they play games, dance, and seek help from a parrot to find their way back home.

source.title: The train journey
source.author: Kanti Jadia
source.illustrator: Deepa Balsavar, Madhuvanti Anantharajan, Preeti Krishnamurthy, Santosh Pujari

stories.summary: Latika, Vidvath, and Shubhi go on a train journey to Gudi Gudi with their parents. They enjoy a meal on the train and later continue their adventure to the mountains by bus.

Bear, a journalist in the Forest-By-The-Sea, struggles to find a 'BREAKING NEWS' story. With the help of Singing Sardarji, Bear discovers his true passion for writing and sets out to explore the world, gathering stories that touch people's hearts.

Golu, a young boy aspiring to be a detective, discovers red umbrellas in the jungle with his magic torch. Among them, he finds a lost little girl who becomes his friend as he promises to help her find her way back home.

During a great famine, a Folklore Singer travels to a haunted village to seek help from his Master's spirit to bring rain to his village. Along the way, he brings a Dinosaur back to life and discovers the power of singing a rainmaking duet with the creature.

source.title: No Tricking Kutti
source.author: Kalyani Radhakrishnan
source.illustrator: Greystroke, Hari Kumar Nair, Mayur Mistry, Nina Sabnani, Suvidha Mistry, Tanvee Nabar

stories.summary: Kutti wakes up confused about how morning comes so quickly. With the help of his grandfather, he learns about time and realizes that God isn't tricking him.
A small kitten shows courage by climbing a tree to eat a fruit but gets stuck when it starts raining. With the help of a boy and a monkey friend, the brave kitten is safely rescued.
A man goes to the forest to practice music and discovers a big mushroom where he can sit and play. As he practices, the birds and animals in the forest start to listen to his music.

A group of children living in an untidy place decide to clean their surroundings to improve living conditions. Despite facing challenges like a barking dog, they persist in their efforts to enhance their health and cleaning skills.
A child goes to school and faces a challenge in math class when their test paper is torn by a mischievous cat. The child must find a solution to the problem before the next day.

source.title: Chameleon Life
source.author: Prateek Chandrawal
source.illustrator: Herminder Ohri, Muniza Shariq, Nirvaan Pahwa, Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'

stories.summary: A Chameleon encounters a snake while sleeping on a tree and must use its color-changing ability to escape. It faces more challenges on its way to find water and a safe place to rest.
